config.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync

intro.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that demonstrates how to keep a user's authentication status synchronized across multiple browser tabs. You will learn the core concept of using browser storage events to communicate state changes between tabs. The main technologies involved are Angular services, localStorage, and the window's storage event listener. By the end, you will understand how to create a seamless multi-tab experience where logging in or out in one tab automatically updates the auth state in all others.
intro.usecase: Multi-tab auth sync is essential for modern web applications where users frequently work across multiple browser tabs. Banking dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and collaborative tools like Google Workspace all require consistent authentication states across tabs. When a user logs out in one tab, all other tabs should immediately reflect this change to prevent unauthorized access. Similarly, session timeouts or permission changes must propagate instantly to maintain security and user experience. This pattern ensures users don't encounter confusing or insecure states when switching between tabs of the same application.

objectives: Implement a service to manage authentication state across browser tabs
Configure event listeners to detect storage changes in other tabs
Initialize authentication state from localStorage on application startup
Bind authentication status updates to UI components in real-time
Manipulate localStorage to synchronize login/logout actions across tabs
Integrate the multi-tab sync service into existing Angular authentication flow
Control authentication state propagation when users interact with multiple tabs

steps.title: Import required Angular modules and services
steps.instruction: Import Component, OnInit, OnDestroy from '@angular/core' and BehaviorSubject from 'rxjs'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from the same module.
steps.seedCode: // Import Component, OnInit, OnDestroy from '@angular/core' and BehaviorSubject from 'rxjs'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular core modules and RxJS BehaviorSubject are imported for building the multi-tab authentication component.
successCriteria: Component, OnInit, and OnDestroy are imported from '@angular/core', and BehaviorSubject is imported from 'rxjs'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some required symbols, but check if you have all four: Component, OnInit, OnDestroy from '@angular/core' and BehaviorSubject from 'rxjs'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import Component, OnInit, OnDestroy from '@angular/core' and BehaviorSubject from 'rxjs'.

steps.title: Create the AuthService with BehaviorSubject
steps.instruction: Create an AuthService class with a private BehaviorSubject property named authState$ to track authentication state.
steps.hint: Define a class called AuthService and inside it, declare a private property authState$ of type BehaviorSubject<boolean>.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an AuthService class with a private BehaviorSubject property initialized to track authentication state.
successCriteria: AuthService class is defined with a private authState$ property of type BehaviorSubject<boolean>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the BehaviorSubject property is private and named authState$.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthService class or the private BehaviorSubject property is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Add login and logout methods to AuthService
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthService class, add a login() method that sets the BehaviorSubject value to true and a logout() method that sets it to false.
steps.hint: Both methods should call this.authState$.next() with the appropriate boolean value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthService will have login() and logout() methods that can change the authentication state.
successCriteria: AuthService contains login() and logout() methods that update authState$ with true and false respectively.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both methods properly update the BehaviorSubject using .next().
steps.feedbackWrong: The methods should update the BehaviorSubject's value. Check that login() sets it to true and logout() to false.

steps.title: Create an observable for authentication state
steps.instruction: In the AuthService class, add a public observable property named isAuthenticated$ that exposes the authentication state for components to subscribe to.
steps.hint: Make the property public and assign it the value of authState$.asObservable() to expose it as a read-only observable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthService will have a public observable property that components can use to subscribe to authentication state changes.
successCriteria: The AuthService has a public isAuthenticated$ observable property that returns authState$.asObservable().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a public property named isAuthenticated$ and assigned it the value of authState$.asObservable().
steps.feedbackWrong: The observable property is not correctly defined. Check that you've added a public isAuthenticated$ property that exposes authState$ as an observable.

steps.title: Implement localStorage synchronization
steps.instruction: In the AuthService class, add a private method named syncWithLocalStorage that reads from localStorage on initialization and writes to localStorage when auth state changes.
steps.hint: Use localStorage.getItem to read the stored value and localStorage.setItem to write. Convert the string value to boolean when reading.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthService now has a private syncWithLocalStorage method that handles reading from and writing to localStorage for authentication state.
successCriteria: AuthService contains a private syncWithLocalStorage method that reads initial auth state from localStorage and subscribes to authState$ to write changes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the method, but make sure it both reads the initial value from localStorage and subscribes to write changes when auth state updates.
steps.feedbackWrong: The syncWithLocalStorage method is missing or incomplete. It should handle both reading initial state from localStorage and writing updates to localStorage.

steps.title: Add storage event listener for cross-tab sync
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthService class, add a private method named 'setupStorageListener' that sets up a window event listener for 'storage' events to update the authState$ BehaviorSubject when other tabs change the authentication state.
steps.hint: Use window.addEventListener('storage', (event) => { ... }) inside the method. Check if the event.key matches your localStorage key (e.g., 'authState') and update authState$.next() with the new value from event.newValue.
steps.expectedOutcome: A private method 'setupStorageListener' is added to AuthService that listens for storage events and updates the authState$ BehaviorSubject when the 'authState' key changes in localStorage.
successCriteria: The AuthService has a private method named 'setupStorageListener' that uses window.addEventListener for 'storage' events, checks for the 'authState' key, and updates authState$.next() with the parsed boolean value from event.newValue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but it may be missing some key elements. Make sure it's a private method named 'setupStorageListener', uses window.addEventListener for 'storage' events, checks if event.key equals 'authState', and updates authState$.next() with the parsed boolean from event.newValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The storage event listener method is not correctly implemented. Review the instruction: you need to add a private method named 'setupStorageListener' that listens for 'storage' events and updates the authState$ BehaviorSubject when the 'authState' key changes.

steps.title: Create the main AppComponent
steps.instruction: Create the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator and a basic template that displays 'Multi-Tab Auth Sync Demo'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define the component. Set the selector to 'app-root' and add a template with an h1 heading.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent is defined with a basic template that will serve as the foundation for the authentication UI.
successCriteria: AppComponent class is created with @Component decorator, selector 'app-root', and template containing 'Multi-Tab Auth Sync Demo'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include the @Component decorator with selector and template properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using the @Component decorator with the required metadata.

steps.title: Inject AuthService into AppComponent
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent constructor, inject the AuthService as a dependency.
steps.hint: Add a constructor parameter with the type AuthService and assign it to a public property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: injecting a service
constructor(private authService: AuthService) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent constructor will have an AuthService parameter, enabling dependency injection.
successCriteria: AuthService is injected as a constructor parameter
The parameter is typed as AuthService
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the constructor parameter has the correct type (AuthService) and is properly declared.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthService injection is missing or incorrect. Check that the constructor parameter is typed as AuthService.

steps.title: Subscribe to authentication state in AppComponent
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent's ngOnInit method, subscribe to the AuthService's isAuthenticated$ observable and update a component property with the authentication state.
steps.hint: Create a property like isAuthenticated in AppComponent, then in ngOnInit subscribe to authService.isAuthenticated$ and assign the value to that property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent will have a property that updates whenever the authentication state changes across tabs.
successCriteria: AppComponent has isAuthenticated property, implements OnInit, and subscribes to authService.isAuthenticated$ in ngOnInit.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're subscribing to authService.isAuthenticated$ and updating the isAuthenticated property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The subscription isn't set up correctly. Check that you're implementing OnInit and subscribing in ngOnInit.

steps.title: Create login and logout buttons in template
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add two buttons: one with the label 'Login' and another with the label 'Logout'.
steps.hint: Add the buttons directly inside the template property of the @Component decorator, after the existing heading.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template will contain two buttons with labels 'Login' and 'Logout'.
successCriteria: Two button elements with the correct labels are present in the AppComponent template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but make sure you have exactly two: one labeled 'Login' and one labeled 'Logout'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required login and logout buttons. Add two button elements with the correct labels.

steps.title: Wire buttons to AuthService methods
steps.instruction: Add click event handlers to the login and logout buttons in the AppComponent template that call the AuthService's login() and logout() methods.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="handler()" on each button. The handlers should call the corresponding methods on the injected authService.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a button to a service method
<button (click)="authService.login()">Login</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The login and logout buttons will be wired to call the AuthService methods when clicked.
successCriteria: The AppComponent template includes buttons with (click) event handlers that call authService.login() and authService.logout().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both buttons have proper (click) handlers that call the correct AuthService methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't properly wired to the AuthService methods. Check that you're using (click) event binding and calling authService.login() and authService.logout().

steps.title: Display authentication status in template
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add a paragraph that displays the current authentication status using the 'isAuthenticated' property.
steps.hint: Use Angular's interpolation syntax {{ }} to display the boolean value in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a boolean value in a template

User is logged in: {{ isLoggedIn }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the authentication status (true/false) below the heading.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added to the template that displays the value of 'isAuthenticated' using interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added content to the template, but make sure it displays the 'isAuthenticated' property value using {{ }} interpolation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet show the authentication status. Add a paragraph that displays the 'isAuthenticated' property value.
